title: Bank of England Bank Rate decision, MPC Summary and minutes, no Monetary Policy Report (12:00 London / 07:00 ET) — the round the first wholly post-Budget labour print precedes by two days
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the Bank's own upcoming-MPC-dates page lists 'Thursday 18 March' among its 2027 dates, marked PROVISIONAL, with the publication set given as MPC Summary and minutes only and NO Monetary Policy Report (the 2027 Report rounds on that page are 4 February and 29 April). Filed estimate on two counts: the Bank calls the date provisional, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the Bank of England. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2027-01-19, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 LANE, 2026-09-09, and it is the SECOND half of a gap rather than an incidental find: this calendar carries boe-decision entries for 2026-12-17, 2027-04-29, 2027-06-17 and 2027-11-04, so BOTH 2027 rounds before April — 4 February and 18 March — were missing while later ones were present. WHY THIS ONE SPECIFICALLY EARNS A SLOT ALONGSIDE 02-04: it is the destination of the proposing lane's headline correction. The UK labour chain has three times described a release as carrying 'the first AWE window wholly after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget' and twice named the wrong release. By the window rule the chain itself verified across four bulletins — the headline average-weekly-earnings window is the three months ending TWO months before the release month — the first wholly post-Budget window is NOV 2026-JAN 2027, and it publishes in the MARCH 2027 release, not the February one. That release is dated '16 March 2027 at 7:00am', status 'Confirmed' on the gov.uk statistics-announcements register fetched 2026-09-09. It therefore precedes THIS round by two days, which is the same D-2 non-Report geometry the uk-labour-market-2026-12-15 lane argued from precedent (the 19 March 2026 and 18 June 2026 non-Report rounds each incorporated a bulletin published five hours earlier). So the first UK labour print that can carry any Budget signal at all arrives D-2 to a non-Report round — worth having on the calendar before a lane needs it, not after. HONEST LIMIT ON THE 'BUDGET SIGNAL' FRAMING: even that release may show nothing, because UK employer-cost measures conventionally take effect the FOLLOWING April (Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs 13.8% to 15% effective April 2025), which is the 11-17 sibling's finding and is not re-derived here. MEDIUM on the same argued grounds as the 02-04 proposal, minus the Report: symbols [], no UK-listed symbol tracked, no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook. PROMOTION CRITERION: the Bank moving this date from provisional to confirmed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
